snap.text: You meant to say it calmly. It came out at a volume that set off a car alarm. Their lip wobbles. Yours does too.

styles.title: The Tag-Teamer
styles.text: You passed the baton. Sometimes it was a relay. Sometimes it was a hot potato. Either way, two of you ran the race.

styles.title: The Negotiator
styles.text: Every snack was a treaty. Every shoe was a summit. You'd be terrifying at a car dealership.

styles.title: The Screen Diplomat
styles.text: A man in corduroy did a lot of your parenting this week. He did it well. You'll deal with the screen-off meltdowns later. You always do.

styles.title: The Martyr
styles.text: You did everything yourself, perfectly, and told no one. Your partner is still not sure what you did all week. Neither is your spine.

styles.title: The Bribe Economist
styles.text: Crackers, stickers, one more episode. The toddler has learned the value of a deal, and the deal has gotten expensive.

styles.title: The Drill Sergeant
styles.text: No meant no. No meant no forty times. The tantrums were loud, but they were short, and they knew where they stood.

modifiers.title: Monday
modifiers.text: Back to it. The weekend was a beautiful lie.

modifiers.title: Work Deadline
modifiers.text: The report is due at 5. Your toddler is due at everything else.

modifiers.title: Daycare Closed: Pink Eye
modifiers.text: Pink eye at daycare. Your toddler is fine. Your toddler is also home all day, touching every surface in the house with intent.

modifiers.title: Date Night
modifiers.text: The sitter arrives at 7:00. The reservation is at 7:30. All you have to do is get through the day with enough left to put on real pants.

modifiers.title: Teething
modifiers.text: A molar is coming in. Your toddler is chewing everything, including grudges.

modifiers.title: Grandma Is Visiting
modifiers.text: Free childcare! Also opinions. So many opinions.

modifiers.title: Potty Training: Day 3
modifiers.text: The internet said it would take three days. It is day 3. The internet lied.

modifiers.title: Sleep Regression
modifiers.text: Your toddler did stand-up comedy from 2 to 4 AM. You slept in installments.

tasks.label: Call the pediatrician about the rash

lifeline.title: Grandma to the Rescue
lifeline.text: You call your mother. She arrives in eleven minutes with a casserole, a bag of cookies and a list of observations. She sends you to bed at 4 PM. You don't argue.

collapse.title: Parent.exe Has Stopped Responding
collapse.text: You sat down on the kitchen floor to tie a shoe and simply did not get up again. Your toddler covers you with a dish towel and says, "Night night." Your partner finds you like that at 6.

talk.title: We Need to Talk
talk.text: Not a fight, exactly. Two people at the kitchen counter, too tired to finish their sentences. The monitor hisses. Neither of you moves. Next week, you'll try the ledger thing.

ballpit.title: The House Has Fallen
ballpit.text: Your home is now an installation. A local gallery calls it "a bold statement on domestic entropy." The couch is under there somewhere.

groupchat.title: Removed From the Group Chat
groupchat.text: "Admin removed you." Three words, forty-one parents. You'll never know when pajama day is again. Your toddler, unaware of your social death, hands you a rock.

sitter_quits.title: The Sitter Quits at the Door
sitter_quits.text: The sitter rings the bell at 7:00. Your toddler answers it, naked, holding a spatula, wide awake. The sitter looks at you, looks at the spatula, and leaves. You eat cereal in your going-out shirt.

couch.title: Asleep in Your Going-Out Shirt
couch.text: You sat down on the couch for one minute to put on your shoes. It is now 9:40 PM. Your partner is asleep next to you, also in a going-out shirt. The reservation called twice.

legend.title: You Remembered You Like Each Other
legend.text: Dessert. A walk. A whole conversation that wasn't about poop. You get home and the toddler is asleep and the sitter says they were "an angel," which is a lie, but a kind one.

solid.title: A Good Week, Actually
solid.text: Dinner was good. You talked about the toddler for forty-one minutes and each other for twenty. That counts. That absolutely counts.

survived.title: You Made It to Friday
survived.text: You made it to the restaurant, mostly awake. You split an appetizer and a yawn. It wasn't magic. It was a table for two, and that's more than last month.

barely.title: Barely, Together
barely.text: You were home by 8:45 and asleep by 8:50, holding hands, fully dressed. The sitter got paid for three hours. Worth it.

events.title: The Monitor Crackles
events.text: A small voice announces, with total confidence, that it is morning. The sun disagrees. The sun is not in charge here.

choices.label: Go get them. Be the morning person.

outcomes.text: You are greeted like a returning war hero. Then asked for a banana. Then told the banana is wrong.

choices.label: Nudge your partner. It's their turn.

outcomes.text: Your partner gets up without a word. They know the ledger. You get nine more minutes and a dream about sleeping.
"I did it yesterday," your partner mumbles, which is technically true. You get up. The banana is still wrong.
You lie in the dark absorbing nine minutes of escalating demands. Technically rest.

events.title: Breakfast Service
events.text: You cut the toast into triangles. Your toddler wanted squares. Your toddler did not say this out loud. You were supposed to know.

outcomes.text: Squares: approved. One bite is taken. The rest goes into the heating vent.
They consider this. They eat a triangle while making eye contact, like a small mob boss.
The triangle hits the floor butter-side down, as physics demands. So does your toddler.
"Organic Harvest Medley." It costs $3.49 and tastes like a wet garden. They love it.

events.title: Full Meltdown
events.text: Something has gone wrong. Maybe the banana. Maybe the concept of time. Your toddler is a boneless puddle on the floor, screaming at a frequency only dogs and parents can hear.

choices.label: Get on the floor and validate their feelings

outcomes.text: "You're frustrated that the sky is the wrong blue." It works. You are covered in floor dust and something like peace.
The man in corduroy sings about feelings. Your toddler becomes a statue. You drink a coffee while it is still technically hot.

choices.label: Wait it out. Become a rock.

outcomes.text: You become a rock. The storm passes, as storms do. Most last only a few minutes. This one felt like a fiscal quarter.

events.title: The Screen-Off Meltdown
events.text: The credits roll. The silence breaks. This one has a second act, a key change and a lighting design.

outcomes.text: Peace, again. You both know how this ends. You both choose not to think about it.
Twenty minutes of grief for a man in corduroy. Then, abruptly, they want a snack. Like nothing happened. Like you didn't just age.

events.title: Nap Time (Allegedly)
events.text: Your toddler's eyes are drooping. Your toddler is also standing in the crib gripping the bars, yelling "I'M NOT TIRED" like an inmate in a prison movie.

choices.label: Full ritual: sleep sack, white noise, the Song

outcomes.text: They're out. You freeze in the hallway, terrified a floorboard will betray you.
Twenty-two minutes. The shortest nap known to science. They wake up refreshed and furious.

choices.label: Car nap: drive until they pass out

outcomes.text: You drive in circles. They sleep. You sit in the driveway with the engine running, eating crackers from the cup holder. Peak living.
The moment the engine stops, their eyes snap open, like a vampire at sundown.

choices.label: Skip it. They said they're not tired.

outcomes.text: You believe them. This is a mistake. But it's a mistake with an extra hour in it.

events.title: Nap Time: Your 90 Minutes
events.text: They're down. You have about an hour and a half. You have nine hours of things to do.

outcomes.text: You wake with the couch's texture printed on your face. You feel like a new person. A new, slightly damp person.
Every surface is clean. You stand there admiring it. You hear a small voice. It's over.

choices.label: Knock out the oldest thing on your list

outcomes.text: Done. Crossed off. You feel a level of satisfaction usually reserved for people who have slept.
You watch a stranger renovate a bathroom for forty minutes. It's the most relaxing thing you've done since 2019.

events.title: "Who Gave Them the iPad?"
events.text: Your partner walks in, holding the iPad, the toddler and a tone. The iPad is sticky. The toddler is wearing yogurt.

choices.label: "That was me. It was a day."

outcomes.text: They put the iPad down. "Yeah. Mine too." A small truce, signed in yogurt.
It lands. It's true and it doesn't help. Dinner is very quiet.
They read it. They go quiet. Then they take bedtime without being asked. You were right. It still costs something.
They read it. It's not as lopsided as you thought. It's lopsided the other way. You both decide to never mention the ledger again.

events.title: The Handoff
events.text: Your partner walks in. The toddler runs to them like they've returned from war. You've been here all day and you are, apparently, furniture.

choices.label: Tag out. Ten minutes alone in the car.

outcomes.text: You sit in the driveway with the engine off, staring at nothing. It is the best ten minutes of your week.

choices.label: Ask about their day. Really ask.

outcomes.text: They talk. You listen. For six minutes you are two adults having a conversation. The toddler interrupts, but the six minutes happened.
You deliver the full incident report. They nod. They had their own day. Nobody wins the who's-more-tired contest. Nobody ever does.

events.title: The Dinner Standoff
events.text: Dinner contains a vegetable. Your toddler examines the plate like a critic who has already decided to write a bad review.

outcomes.text: A real dinner, with colors. Your toddler eats the bread. You eat the colors. Everyone is fed, technically.
Plain buttered noodles: the official cuisine of toddlerhood. Somewhere, a nutritionist feels a disturbance.
The delivery driver knows your name. The delivery driver knows your toddler's name. This is fine.

events.title: Bedtime: The Final Boss
events.text: It's 7:30. Pajamas are on, after a ten-minute chase. Teeth are brushed: one tooth, briefly. Now comes the negotiation.

choices.label: Full routine: three books, two songs

outcomes.text: Three books become five. Two songs become an encore. But their eyes are closing, and they tell you they love you.
Your partner takes bedtime. You hear the songs through the wall. You lie on the couch, eyes closed, a free person.
"I did it last night." They didn't. You don't have the energy to argue. You do bedtime.
Silence. You don't trust it, so you do the dishes on high alert.
The door clicks shut. A small voice: "I need to tell you something." It's about a dog they saw in April.

events.title: The Early Bedtime
events.text: It's Friday. The sitter comes at 7. The toddler must be asleep by then, which means bedtime is now, which the toddler can smell.

outcomes.text: Warm bath. One book, read at auctioneer speed. One song, abridged. Their eyes go heavy. Yours do too. Not yet.
You do the bath. They do the book. It runs like a pit crew. You high-five in the hallway like idiots.
You both do the bath and neither does the book, and you argue in whispers about whose job the book was.

choices.label: Drive around until they pass out

outcomes.text: Two laps of the neighborhood. Asleep in the car seat. The transfer to the crib is a bomb disposal operation.

events.title: Can You Even Go?
events.text: It's 7:00. The doorbell rings. The reservation is at 7:30. Your going-out shirt has a stain you have decided is a pattern.

outcomes.text: Liquid courage. Your eyes open a little wider. Tonight's sleep will pay for this, but tonight is tonight.
You lie on the bed fully dressed and set three alarms. You wake up confused but upright.
Shoes. Keys. Door. You're out before anyone can ask you for anything.

events.title: Table for Two
events.text: You made it. Candles. Real napkins. Nobody is throwing anything. You both stare at the menu like it's a foreign country.

choices.label: Talk about anything but the toddler

outcomes.text: You last eleven minutes. Then you show each other photos of the toddler. Then your partner says, "Hey. I missed you."
You try. The silences are long. Then you both laugh at the same terrible thing at the next table, and it's almost like before.
Dessert. A second glass. A walk home the long way. You will be destroyed tomorrow. Tomorrow is Saturday.

events.title: Diaper Math
events.text: You open the box. There are four diapers left. You do the math. The math is bad.

outcomes.text: Subscribe and save. Arriving tomorrow. You are an adult who handles things.

choices.label: Text your partner to grab some

outcomes.text: "On it 👍" They will absolutely forget. Wait, no. They send a photo of the receipt. Who is this person?
Read at 2:14 PM. No reply. The diapers remain theoretical.
Four is plenty. Four is a number. Nothing bad has ever happened with four.

events.title: There Are No Diapers
events.text: "Buy diapers" expired. It's evening. There is one diaper left and the toddler has plans for it.

outcomes.text: You buy diapers in slippers under fluorescent lights. The cashier has seen this before. The cashier has seen everything.

choices.label: "Whose turn was it to buy them?"

outcomes.text: It was yours. It was on your list. You both know it. The argument is about something else, as they always are.

events.title: "Did You RSVP?"
events.text: Theo's mom texts the group chat: "Still waiting on a few RSVPs 🙂". The smiley face is doing a lot of work.

outcomes.text: "So sorry!! Crazy week!!" Two exclamation points. The universal sign of a parent drowning politely.

events.title: The Form
events.text: Daycare calls. The form was due this morning. Your child cannot go on the field trip to the pumpkin patch without it, and will be told why.

outcomes.text: You hand-deliver a form like it's a subpoena. The teacher's smile is very patient.

events.title: The Rash, Revisited
events.text: You never called about the rash. The rash has opinions now.

outcomes.text: The nurse is calm and kind and says it's probably eczema. You feel a rush of gratitude so big it's embarrassing.

events.title: Overdue
events.text: The library emails. The books are overdue. One of them is now partially eaten.

choices.label: Pay the fine. Accept your shame.

outcomes.text: $11.40 for a book about a bear who is also tired. You get it, bear.

events.title: It's Quiet. Too Quiet.
events.text: The living room has been silent for six minutes. Silence, in this house, is never good news.

outcomes.text: You catch them uncapping a permanent marker, eyes locked on a fresh white wall. You confiscate it. Crisis averted. This time.
You finish your coffee. It's lovely. It's the last lovely thing for a while.

events.title: The Sharpie Incident
events.text: The hallway is now a mural titled "Untitled (Permanent)."

outcomes.text: Magic eraser, elbow grease, and words you bleep in your head. It's mostly gone. Mostly.
"Our little Basquiat 🎨" Forty likes. One comment asking if it's washable. It is not.

choices.label: Leave it. Deal with it Friday.

outcomes.text: It's a feature wall now. You walk past it eleven times today. It looks at you every time.

events.title: You Said the Word
events.text: Lego, bare foot, 3 PM. You said a word. A [BLEEP] word. Your toddler said it back, perfectly, and is now saying it to the dog. You don't have a dog.

outcomes.text: It will come up again. At daycare. To the director. You know this the way you know the sun will rise.

events.title: The Stomach Bug Has Entered the Chat
events.text: It started with one ominous burp. It ended with you holding a mixing bowl like a goalie. It is coming for you next.

outcomes.text: Every surface, every toy, every doorknob. You smell like a public pool. It might not be enough.
You lay towels like a field medic. The laundry pile reaches a height that requires a permit.

events.title: "You're My Best Friend."
events.text: Out of nowhere, mid-snack, they pat your face with a hand covered in hummus and say it. Then they go back to the snack like nothing happened.

outcomes.text: "!!!!!" they reply, from a meeting. Then a heart. Then: "I'm so jealous."
You don't post it. You don't tell anyone. You just keep it.

events.title: Coffee, Attempt #3
events.text: You've reheated this coffee so many times it's legally a soup.

outcomes.text: You drink it hot. A single tear rolls down your cheek.
A fresh pot. You smell it. You feel briefly human.

choices.label: Skip it. Hydrate like an adult.

outcomes.text: Water. How novel. Your body doesn't know what to do with it.

events.title: A Quiet Moment
events.text: Your toddler is sitting calmly in a corner. When they see you, they say, "I didn't do it." You don't know what "it" is.

outcomes.text: It was the lipstick. It was always going to be the lipstick.

choices.label: Don't ask questions you don't want answered

outcomes.text: You'll find out at 4 PM. It involves the toilet.

events.title: The Crib Whisper
events.text: 2:47 AM. A small figure is standing in the crib whispering your name at the wall. You're about 70% sure this isn't a ghost.

outcomes.text: Twenty minutes of the shush-pat. They go down. You lie awake for forty more, because your body thinks it's a job now.
Your partner gets up without a word. The ledger is a powerful document.
"I got the last two," they whisper. They did. You get up.
The whispering stops. You listen to the silence like it's a symphony.
The whispering becomes yelling. You both get up. Nobody wins.

events.title: You Replay It. Again.
events.text: 3:12 AM. You're replaying the moment you snapped today. In the replay you are calm and wise. In real life you were not.

choices.label: Wake your partner to talk about it

outcomes.text: They listen, half asleep. "You're a good parent," they mumble. "Everyone yells." It helps more than it should. Now you're both awake.

choices.label: Look up how to repair it

outcomes.text: The article says repair matters more than perfection. Tomorrow you'll say sorry. They'll say "OK" and ask for a snack.

events.title: Nothing
events.text: 2 AM, 3 AM, 4 AM. Nothing. The monitor is silent. You wake up every hour anyway, to check that the nothing is still happening.

outcomes.text: You almost don't trust it. Almost.

events.title: Bath Time
events.text: Bath time. It will be either the best thing that has ever happened to them or a human rights violation. You won't know which until the water's running, and by then it's too late.

choices.label: Bubbles, toys, the full spa treatment

outcomes.text: Half the water ends up on the floor. The bathroom smells like "Lavender Dreams." Your socks are wet forever. But they're yawning.

choices.label: Your partner's on bath. They promised.

outcomes.text: A promise, kept, with a timestamp. You hear splashing, singing and one "oh, come ON." You lie on the hallway floor like a starfish.

choices.label: Ask your partner to do bath

outcomes.text: Your partner does the math. The math is not in their favor. They roll up their sleeves without a word.
"Can you do it?" "Can YOU?" You do it. You forget the bubbles. "WHERE ARE THE BUBBLES." Not a question.

choices.label: Skip it. They're clean enough. Probably.

outcomes.text: There's yogurt in their hair, which is basically conditioner. A daycare teacher will notice. Daycare teachers notice everything.

events.title: The Wrong Cup
events.text: You poured the milk into the blue cup. Your toddler wanted the blue cup. But not like this.

outcomes.text: The green cup is accepted. You're a hostage negotiator now. The hostage is you.

choices.label: Hold firm. Blue is a perfectly good cup.

outcomes.text: They drink from the blue cup while staring at you the entire time, like a very small mob boss. Boundary: held.
The milk goes on the floor. "I want the blue cup," they sob, holding the blue cup. The forums would be proud of you. The floor is not.

choices.label: Pour it into the green cup, then back into the blue one

outcomes.text: The milk has been purified by its journey. It is now acceptable. You don't know what you did, but you'll do it again.
"That's green milk now," they explain, slowly, like you're the toddler.

events.title: Getting Dressed
events.text: Your toddler will get dressed on one condition: rain boots, one sock, a tutu and a Halloween costume from two years ago that no longer fits. These terms are final. Everything is final until it isn't.

outcomes.text: You'll call it "self-expression." A stranger at the store compliments the look. The stranger is lying, and you both know it.

choices.label: Negotiate down to just the boots

outcomes.text: Fifteen minutes of tense diplomacy. The boots stay. The costume goes. Both sides claim victory, like a real summit, with about as much crying.

choices.label: Insist on the outfit you picked

outcomes.text: You win. They're wearing your outfit. They're also lying face-down in the hallway like a starfish that has given up.
They comply, then give you the silent treatment. It lasts four minutes, which in toddler years is a prison sentence.

events.title: Code Brown
events.text: A diaper situation has escalated beyond the diaper. It's up the back. It's in the onesie. Holy crap, and that is not a figure of speech. Is it on the ceiling fan? Don't think about the ceiling fan.

choices.label: Peel the onesie down over the shoulders, medic-style

outcomes.text: Those envelope shoulders exist for exactly this. Nobody tells you until you need it. You feel like a surgeon. The onesie dies a hero.
A bonus bath. The tub is a crime scene. The rubber duck has seen things it can't unsee. The toddler, however, is delighted.

choices.label: Text your partner a photo. For the record.

outcomes.text: "OH NO," then "you're a hero," then a heart. You feel briefly, chemically appreciated. It doesn't clean anything.
"lol." Just "lol." You will be thinking about that "lol" at your retirement party.

choices.label: Call your partner in to "see something"

outcomes.text: They look at you, then at the ledger on the fridge, then take the onesie. You love them. You'll say so later. Maybe.
They assess the situation and slowly back out of the room, like it's a bear. You are alone. You were always alone.

events.title: Content Opportunity
events.text: Your toddler is doing something genuinely adorable with a wooden spoon. This could be content. The algorithm is hungry. The algorithm is always hungry.

choices.label: Stage the perfect photo for the feed

outcomes.text: Shot 47 is usable once you crop out the laundry. Caption: "Slow mornings 🤍". Nothing about this morning was slow.
You watch. You don't post. It's lovely, and nobody will ever know it happened, which bothers you more than it should.

choices.label: Post it with a long caption about being present

outcomes.text: "I put my phone away to be present," you type, on your phone. 214 likes. You check all 214.
Top comment: "is that spoon BPA-free?" You spend nine minutes drafting a reply. You delete it. You draft another.

events.title: Can Everyone See My Screen?
events.text: You have a call, cameras on, "it's a culture thing." Your partner, working from home today, has a call in the next room. Your toddler is wearing a colander and no pants. Somebody has to take the colander.

choices.label: Take the toddler. Your call can be audio-only.

outcomes.text: You present with your camera off and a toddler on your lap, saying "great point" into the mute button. Your partner mouths "thank you" through the glass. You will be bringing this up later.

choices.label: "Mine's a client. Yours is a stand-up."

outcomes.text: They do the ledger math in their head and take the toddler. Their stand-up is attended by a colander. Your client never knows.
"My stand-up is with the VP." A standoff. The toddler settles it by attending both calls, in sequence, pantsless.

choices.label: Keep presenting. Pretend nothing is happening.

outcomes.text: You present the Q3 roadmap while a pantsless figure in a colander does laps behind you. Nobody mentions it. Your manager says, "Love the energy."

choices.label: Hand over a snack and mute yourself

outcomes.text: Mute. Unmute: "Great point." Mute. The toddler eats crackers in your doorway like a raccoon at a campsite. The keyboard gets some too.

events.title: The Screen
events.text: Your toddler requests "Sunshine Sing-Along," in which a man in an alarming amount of corduroy sings about feelings. It's 22 minutes long. You could do so much in 22 minutes.

choices.label: Put it on. You need this.

outcomes.text: You fold a load of laundry, answer three emails and stare at a wall for a while. Somewhere, a study you'll never read is judging you.

choices.label: No screens. Make a sensory bin.

outcomes.text: You fill a bin with dry rice. Within seconds the rice is not in the bin. The rice is everywhere. The rice is eternal. You mention it in the group chat anyway.
They learn that a man in corduroy can rhyme "feelings" with "ceilings" four times. You learn nothing. You rest, which is better.
They go play. Independently. For eleven whole minutes. You don't move in case it breaks the spell.
They lie on the floor and whisper "Sunshine" 61 times, softer each time, like a ghost with one word.

events.title: Snack O'Clock
events.text: "Snack," says your toddler. They ate four minutes ago. They are 80% snack and 20% opinion, and the opinion is also about snacks.

outcomes.text: Seven crackers get eaten. Twelve go into the couch. The couch is very well fed.
They eat one slice and declare war on the rest. Still counts. You're counting.
Each slice gets exactly one bite and is handed back to you, like a cat delivering gifts.
You hold the line. They lie face-down on the kitchen floor until a better offer comes along. None does. Eventually they get up like nothing happened.

events.title: The Climber
events.text: Your toddler has climbed the bookshelf and is standing on top, triumphant, like a tiny mountaineer. You did anchor that bookshelf. Right? Right?

outcomes.text: Rescued. They immediately start climbing again. This is their sport now, and you're the unpaid spotter.

choices.label: Get them down, then anchor every dresser in the house

outcomes.text: An hour of drilling into studs while your toddler "helps." Every dresser in the house is anchored to the wall. You're a safety hero. Your lower back has filed a complaint.

choices.label: Get them down, then build a cushion climbing zone

outcomes.text: The couch is now an obstacle course. You will never reassemble it correctly. They climb happily until they're yawning.

events.title: Playground Politics
events.text: At the playground, another parent is watching you like a hall monitor. Their child is eating quinoa from a bento box. Yours is eating sand.

choices.label: Remove the sand. Produce a healthy snack.

outcomes.text: You present your emergency apple. It's bruised. The other parent's eyebrow climbs a full centimeter. Still: an apple.

choices.label: Wipe their face, then hold eye contact and eat your snack

outcomes.text: You eat a granola bar while holding eye contact. It's a power move. It's also, technically, your lunch.
Turns out they're also falling apart. Their kid bit someone yesterday. You exchange numbers. You will never text. It still helps.
Thirty minutes on their "screen-free, sugar-free, nap-optimized" philosophy. Then their kid takes your kid's shovel, and they call it "exploring ownership."

events.title: Aisle Seven
events.text: Your toddler has spotted a cereal with a cartoon on the box, no nutrition and 100% marshmallow. Marketing departments do their best work exactly 34 inches off the ground.

outcomes.text: You leave with the cereal and a small, smug passenger. The cashier says, "You've got your hands full!" Thank you, cashier. Noted.
They accept it. Nearby shoppers nod. You are a legend in aisle seven.
A full floor-level protest. An older shopper tells you to "enjoy every moment." Two other parents give you a solemn nod of solidarity.

choices.label: Distract them with a free bakery balloon

outcomes.text: The balloon works for four minutes. Then it floats away across the store, past every other family. Grief is a lesson, you suppose.

events.title: Script Check
events.text: Your toddler hits you with a toy truck. The parenting account you follow says to "name the feeling and hold the boundary." It has no guidance about the truck.

choices.label: "I won't let you hit. You're having big feelings."

outcomes.text: It works! They hug you. Then they hit you again, gently, to check the boundary's load rating.
"I'm not having big feelings," they say, and hit you with the truck again, with big feelings.
The truck is confiscated. A new war begins over the truck's location. It's on top of the fridge. Everyone knows it's on top of the fridge.

choices.label: Say "OW" like it's a soap opera

outcomes.text: They find this hilarious. You have a new job: saying "ow" dramatically. It pays the same as the old one.
They find it hilarious and want an encore. With the bigger truck. Of course there's a bigger truck.

events.title: The Group Chat
events.text: The parents' group chat has 47 new messages. Someone is asking if it's normal that their two-year-old reads. Someone else is selling a $380 "learning tower," barely used, like everything.

outcomes.text: Three hearts and a reply: "omg mine won't wear clothes either." You feel seen. You feel, briefly, like a person with friends.
Peace. You'll miss the announcement that pajama day moved to Tuesday. You'll find out on Wednesday, the hard way.

choices.label: Ask for advice about the tantrums

outcomes.text: Fourteen replies, all contradicting each other. One just says "essential oils." One is a link to a $200 course.
Someone replies "same." Someone else sends a GIF of a screaming raccoon. That's all you needed.

events.title: Experts Say
events.text: A new study says children who hear "no" too often grow up anxious. Another says children who don't hear it grow up to yell at waiters. Both studies turn out to be the same comment thread.

outcomes.text: You add it to the list of things to feel bad about. The list is a scroll now. At least you can quote it at the next playdate.
You close it. You open another one. It's about screen time. You close that one harder.

events.title: Experts Say
events.text: Sleep experts recommend 11 to 14 hours of sleep per 24 hours for ages 1 to 2, naps included. They didn't say which hours. Your toddler has chosen different ones.

outcomes.text: You do the math on your own sleep. You stop doing the math. You'll quote the real number at the next playdate, unprompted.

choices.label: Send it to your partner. No comment.

outcomes.text: They reply with their own number. It's lower than yours. You feel a rush of something that's either love or solidarity. At this point, same thing.
They reply with their own number. It's lower than yours. Now it's a competition. Nobody wins a sleep competition.

events.title: Experts Say
events.text: Experts say a child may need to try a new food 8 to 10 times, or more, before accepting it. You're on attempt eleven with broccoli. The broccoli is on attempt eleven with the floor.

outcomes.text: Persistence: the only parenting technique with actual evidence behind it and zero glamour.
You blend broccoli into a muffin. They eat the top, leave the bottom and look at you like they know. They know.
Buttered noodles. Plain bread. A cracker. The beige years come for everyone. You'll try broccoli again when you're stronger.

events.title: Influencers Say
events.text: An influencer with perfectly beige toys says, "There are no bad days, only learning days." The influencer has a nanny, a housekeeper and a ring light. You have a learning day every day.

outcomes.text: Unfollowed. The algorithm immediately recommends their sister.
You now know their kids' names, their dog's name and their kitchen better than your own. You can discuss them in the group chat with real authority.

events.title: Partner Check-In
events.text: Your partner texts from work: "How's it going? 😊" There is yogurt on the wall. Your toddler is wearing a cat-food bowl as a hat. You don't have a cat.

outcomes.text: The lie is effortless. The emoji is load-bearing. Your partner will come home believing in a day that did not happen.

choices.label: Send a photo of the yogurt wall

outcomes.text: "OMG. Hang in there. Proud of you." Seven words and you could cry. You might. You don't have time.
"lol," they reply. You will remember this "lol" for decades.
You narrate the entire morning, with sound effects. They reply with a thumbs-up. You have been thumbed.
"Yes. Obviously. I owe you about nine baths." You screenshot it. The timestamp is visible. This is how treaties work.
"Didn't I do it last night?" They did. You'd forgotten. Now you both feel weird about the ledger.

events.title: "Did I Not Mention the Dinner?"
events.text: Your partner texts: the client dinner is tonight. It's been on the calendar for weeks. Their calendar. Attached: a photo of a bread basket. "Home by 7:15, SO sorry."

outcomes.text: You are the bigger person. The bigger person will be eating fish sticks over the sink at 6:40, standing up, like a horse.

choices.label: Send a photo of the yogurt wall. No caption.

outcomes.text: They call from the restaurant hallway to apologize. They're bringing you the tiramisu. The toddler hangs up on them.
"Wow. OK." Then nothing until 7:15. The bread basket goes unaddressed.
Three words. Fair, and you both know it. They reply with a paragraph. You don't read the paragraph. You feel fantastic for about a minute.

events.title: Grandma Has Notes
events.text: Grandma watches your toddler eat a cracker off the floor. "In my day," she begins, "we didn't have all these rules, and you turned out fine." She looks at you. She pauses a little too long.

outcomes.text: You nod. Grandma continues. You learn that car seats are "a racket." (They are not. Keep using the car seat.)
Grandma listens. Grandma nods. Grandma gives the toddler a cookie while maintaining eye contact with you.

choices.label: Let Grandma take over for an hour

outcomes.text: You nap like the dead. You wake to a toddler who has eaten three cookies and learned a new word. You don't know which word. You'll find out at daycare.

events.title: The Broken Banana
events.text: You peeled the banana. You were supposed to let them peel the banana. The banana is broken now. The banana cannot be fixed. Your toddler is in mourning.

outcomes.text: Against all odds, the taped banana is accepted. You post it. Other parents call you "resourceful." You are a banana surgeon.
They see through it instantly. "That's a FAKE banana." They're not wrong.

choices.label: Get a new banana and let them peel it

outcomes.text: They peel it. They take one bite and hand it to you. You eat four bananas a day now. You are mostly banana.

choices.label: "I hear that you're sad the banana broke."

outcomes.text: They nod solemnly. "Banana broke," they agree. A moment of shared grief. A nearby parent looks impressed.
"BANANA BROKE," they agree, at full volume, for nine minutes. Still: textbook validation. The account you follow would be proud.

events.title: The Potty Announcement
events.text: "I need to go potty!" This could be the breakthrough. It could also be the ninth false alarm since lunch. You've stopped being able to tell. So have they.

outcomes.text: SUCCESS. You throw a three-minute celebration with a dance and a sticker. You have never been prouder of anything, including your career.
False alarm. Then a real alarm, two minutes later, on the rug.
They were sure.
They were not sure. They just wanted to flush. Repeatedly. Forever.

choices.label: Diaper back on. Try again next month.

outcomes.text: Nobody has to know. Everybody will know. The internet said you'd be tempted, and the internet, for once, was right.

events.title: Art Hour
events.text: A craft board online says toddlers love "process art." You put out washable paint. "Washable" is a promise, not a guarantee.

outcomes.text: Paint is on the paper, the table, the chair, the toddler and, inexplicably, the inside of the fridge.

choices.label: Crayons only, strapped into the high chair

outcomes.text: They eat the purple one. You check the box: non-toxic. You breathe again. You check the box again.
It's beautiful. A handprint turkey. You made it, using their hand. They were not consulted. 96 likes.

events.title: The Clean-Up Song
events.text: You start the clean-up song. The clean-up song is a lie. Nobody cleans up. The song just informs everyone that a mess exists.

outcomes.text: Done. Your toddler watches, then dumps the bin out again, like a performance artist critiquing your labor.
"Who can put the most blocks in?" It works! You'll try it again tomorrow and it will never work again.
The game is now "who can throw the blocks farthest." Your toddler is winning. Your toddler is always winning.

choices.label: Accept the mess as a lifestyle

outcomes.text: You step on a block and don't even flinch. You are beyond pain now. The house is beyond you.

events.title: Why?
events.text: "Why is the sky?" "Why do dogs?" "Why is Tuesday?" You've answered 34 whys since breakfast. Number 35 is: "Why are you sad?"

outcomes.text: "Because I'm tired." "Why?" You don't have an answer to that one. They pat your knee like a very small therapist.
You have become your parents. It took 34 whys. Your parents lasted 31.
They deliver a six-minute lecture about a dinosaur named Gary. It's nonsense. It's delightful.
They answer "why?" with "why?" Now you're both trapped in the loop, like a philosophy department.

events.title: Package Delivery
events.text: It's here: the $89 wooden rainbow you bought because an account said it "supports open-ended play." Your toddler ignores it and plays with the box. The box was free.

choices.label: Let them play with the box

outcomes.text: The box is a car, a house, a hat and eventually a snack. The rainbow goes on a shelf. For display. For the photos.

choices.label: Stage a photo with the rainbow

outcomes.text: "Open-ended play 🌈" gets 180 likes. Off camera, the rainbow has been thrown at the cat you don't have.
You return the rainbow in a different box, because the original box is now a car. The refund takes 14 business days. The car stays.

events.title: Library Story Time
events.text: Story time at the library. Every toddler is sitting on a carpet square except yours, who is conducting the story like an orchestra.

choices.label: Wrangle them onto a carpet square

outcomes.text: Seated, eventually. Facing the wrong way. Arms folded. A tiny union protest.
The librarian smiles the way people smile at weather. Another parent mouths, "Same."
You fake a phone call and leave at a speed-walk. You wave goodbye to no one. No one waves back.

events.title: The Molars Are Coming
events.text: A molar is fighting its way through. Your toddler is chewing on everything: the remote, your shoulder, the concept of comfort.

outcomes.text: The washcloth is gnawed like a dog's favorite bone. Relief, for about forty minutes. There is drool on every surface you own.

choices.label: Pain reliever, exactly as the label directs

outcomes.text: You check the dosing chart three times and call the nurse line to confirm, as one does. Twenty minutes later: relief, for both of you.

choices.label: Let them chew on your finger

outcomes.text: You learn that molars are sharp. You learn it from the wrong end. You say a word. The word is [BLEEP].

events.title: Snot Situation
events.text: Daycare is closed for pink eye. Your toddler doesn't have pink eye. Your toddler does have a bonus cold, and would rather wipe it on your sleeve than let you near it. Your sleeve is a tissue now.

outcomes.text: It's effective. It's horrifying. They will not forgive you until dinner. They will, however, sleep better tonight.
By lunch, every surface in the house has been personally initialed.

choices.label: Tissues, a song and a lot of patience

outcomes.text: You invent a song about noses. It has four verses. They let you wipe on verse three. Partial credit.

events.title: A Quick Walk
events.text: You leave for a ten-minute walk. Your toddler finds a stick. Then a rock. Then an ant. It's been 45 minutes and you're 30 feet from your front door.

outcomes.text: You learn the name of every rock on the block. They are all named "Rock." It's the best 45 minutes of your week, and you'll never admit it.
They ride like a tiny emperor, pointing at things that please them.
They refuse the stroller. Then they refuse to walk. You carry the toddler AND push an empty stroller, like a parade nobody asked for.

events.title: Your Phone Is Missing
events.text: Your phone is gone. You last saw it in your toddler's hands. They were saying "call Grandma" and walking toward the bathroom.

outcomes.text: It's in the toilet. It's "water-resistant." You learn exactly what that means. You say a word. The word is [BLEEP].
Not in the toilet! It's in the oven. The oven is off. You order an oven lock before you even pick the phone up.
It rings from inside the toy box. A small voice answers: "Hello?" It was a work call. They answered your work call. They were great, honestly.

choices.label: Let it go. You're free now.

outcomes.text: For forty minutes you're unreachable, like a person in 1997. It's wonderful. Then the group chat assumes you're dead.

events.title: Unsolicited Advice
events.text: A stranger in the coffee line looks at your toddler and says, "Shouldn't they have a hat on?" It's 74 degrees.

outcomes.text: Polite. Dignified. Your eye twitches exactly once.
Bold. Unprecedented. The stranger takes their latte and leaves. You feel ten feet tall for the rest of the line.

choices.label: Put a hat on them to end the conversation

outcomes.text: You put a hat on them. They take it off. You put it back on. The stranger nods like a parole officer.

events.title: The Witching Hour
events.text: Late afternoon. Everyone in the house is falling apart at once, a phenomenon parents call "the witching hour" and toddlers call "Tuesday."

outcomes.text: You play the same song fourteen times in a row. You'll hear it in your sleep, if you ever sleep again.

choices.label: Hide in the bathroom for 90 seconds

outcomes.text: You sit on the closed lid, scrolling. A tiny hand appears under the door. A whisper: "I see you."
Cheese, crackers, grapes cut lengthwise, one pickle. You call it tapas. Everyone calms down. Nobody will eat dinner now.

choices.label: Hand the toddler to your partner. Immediately.

outcomes.text: Your partner takes one look at your face and takes the toddler. No questions. You'd marry them all over again, if either of you had the energy.
"I literally just walked in." They did. You both stand in the kitchen, losing, in stereo.

events.title: The Danger Nap
events.text: Late afternoon, driving home. In the mirror, your toddler's eyes are closing. If they sleep now, bedtime moves to 11 PM. If they don't, you have to keep them awake for twelve more minutes.

outcomes.text: You perform every verse of a farm song, including animals you made up. They stay awake. Barely. So do you.

choices.label: Let them sleep. It's so peaceful.

outcomes.text: You sit with them in the parked car, in the driveway, for twenty-five glorious minutes of silence. You'll pay for this at 9:30 PM, with interest.

choices.label: Gently boop their foot every 30 seconds

outcomes.text: They stay awake and are personally offended. You can feel it from the front seat.
They doze off anyway, for four minutes. A power nap. They now have the energy of a golden retriever.

events.title: The Birthday Party
events.text: A two-year-old's birthday party. Theme: "Organic Woodland Minimalism." The invitation had a QR code. The gift registry had a $140 rug on it.

choices.label: Go, with the rug from the registry

outcomes.text: Balloon arch. A hired "wellness magician." A cake made of dates. Your toddler spends the party lying face-down on the rug you bought, which is the only review that matters.

choices.label: Go, with a store-bought sheet cake

outcomes.text: Your blue-frosted sheet cake is placed at the far end of the table, like a quarantined guest. Every kid eats it anyway.
The kids mob your cake. The parents eat it too, secretly, behind the balloon arch. You are a hero of the resistance.
The universal parent code for "no." Everyone knows. Nobody says. You spend the afternoon in sweatpants, like a free person.

events.title: Shoes On
events.text: You need to leave the house, which means shoes. Your toddler has decided that shoes are a government conspiracy and that you're in on it.

outcomes.text: It's a game now, and you're losing. You catch them by the ankles. Shoes on. Wrong feet. Close enough.
A barefoot toddler in public: the official uniform of "we're doing our best." The shoes ride in your pocket like hostages.
Rain boots. It's sunny and 74 degrees. They look happy and damp.
"One..." The shoes go on. You never find out what happens at three. Neither do they.
You reach three. Nothing happens at three. Everyone learns something, mostly them.

events.title: Where Is Bun-Bun?
events.text: Bun-Bun, the stuffed rabbit without whom sleep is impossible, is missing. Bun-Bun was last seen at the grocery store. Or in the car. Or in the void. Bedtime is coming. Bedtime is always coming.

outcomes.text: Bun-Bun is in the freezer. You don't ask. Bun-Bun doesn't say.
No Bun-Bun. At 11 PM you'll be searching the laundry with a flashlight, whispering "where the [BLEEP] are you."

choices.label: Present Backup Bun-Bun with total confidence

outcomes.text: Accepted! Years of secretly buying duplicates finally pay off. You are a criminal mastermind.
"That's not Bun-Bun," they whisper, like a detective in a crime show. They're right. It's Bun-Bun Two.

choices.label: Put your partner on the case

outcomes.text: Your partner finds Bun-Bun in the car seat in four minutes and gloats for nine. Worth it.
"Where did YOU last have it?" It's not a question. It's a closing argument. Bun-Bun stays missing for another hour.

events.title: The Laundry Mountain
events.text: The clean laundry on the couch has achieved sentience. It's taller than your toddler, who is climbing it like a summit. Some of it has been clean since last Thursday.

outcomes.text: Thirty minutes. Every item folded. Your toddler unfolds the towels as you go, like a tiny critic of your work.
The laundry is now a fort. It's no longer clean in any spiritual sense. Everyone is happy.

choices.label: Move the pile to the bed. Problem solved.

outcomes.text: At 10 PM your partner finds it on the bed. You move it back to the couch together, in silence. This cycle is older than both of you.

events.title: Sixty-Four Unread
events.text: The report is due at 5. Your inbox has 64 unread, nine flagged urgent and one titled "Quick question" that is not quick. Your toddler has brought you a shoe and would like you to wear it on your head while you work.

choices.label: Wear the shoe. Answer emails one-handed.

outcomes.text: You clear 31 emails with a sneaker on your head, then forget it's there for your next call. Nobody says anything. Someone in Finance reacts with a single 👟.

choices.label: Mark all 64 as read. Fresh start.

outcomes.text: One click. It feels incredible, like a cold shower for your brain. Two of the 64 were from daycare. One said you're bringing snacks for Thursday. You are now bringing snacks for Thursday.

choices.label: Ask your partner to take the toddler until lunch

outcomes.text: They close their laptop, pick up the toddler and the shoe, and go. You answer emails like a machine built for it. They don't say "you owe me." They don't have to.
"I have the all-hands at 10." They do. They've mentioned it four times this week. You both stand in the hallway holding opposite ends of the same tiredness.

events.title: The Afternoon Wall
events.text: The report needs two more hours of brain. You have about twenty minutes of brain left. The coffee maker sits on the counter, humming softly, like it already knows how this ends.

choices.label: Fourth coffee. Tonight is tomorrow's problem.

outcomes.text: You type with the focus of a jewel thief and the pulse of a hummingbird. The report jumps to 80%. At 11 PM you'll be wide awake, explaining it to your partner, who is asleep.

choices.label: Ask your partner to take the toddler for an hour

outcomes.text: They take the toddler to the park. You write in a silent house, then sit very still for six minutes, listening to the fridge. It sounds like the ocean.
"I've got a 3:30." It's on the shared calendar, in the color you agreed was theirs. You write the rest with a toddler braiding yogurt into your hair.

choices.label: Cold water on the face. Finish it on fumes.

outcomes.text: It's good, actually. You'd celebrate, but standing up makes the room tilt like a boat, so you celebrate sitting down, quietly, with a cracker.

events.title: Due at 5
events.text: The report is 80% done and 100% due at 5. Your toddler has found the laptop's power button. It glows. They love it. Every time they touch it, you make a sound you didn't know you could make.

choices.label: Power through, toddler on your lap

outcomes.text: You type with your arms out like a T. rex so they fit in the gap. Submitted at 4:58. On page 6 there's a "jjjjjjjjj" you won't find until the meeting about it.
The man in corduroy sings about sharing. You write like the building is on fire. Submitted at 4:31, which is early, which nobody will ever notice.
"Happy to discuss!" is corporate for "I know." Your manager replies "Thanks!" and nothing else. You will think about that exclamation point all night.

events.title: Cabin Fever
events.text: Daycare is closed until the class is "symptom-free." You've read the truck book 19 times today. You've built the same tower 31 times so it could be knocked down 31 times. The walls are getting closer.

choices.label: Build a blanket fort. Commit to the bit.

outcomes.text: Four chairs, every blanket you own and a flashlight. Inside, your toddler whispers like you're both hiding from someone. You stay in there much longer than you meant to.
The man in corduroy sings about rainy days. You eat crackers over the kitchen sink, standing up, which is your version of a spa day.
They play beside you, narrating everything, for fourteen whole minutes. You sit. You don't talk. It's the best meeting you've had all week.
Quiet time lasts 90 seconds, then becomes loud time, on your lap, with a drum.

events.title: Wash Everything on Hot
events.text: The daycare email says to wash "all bedding, towels and soft toys" on hot. Mr. Blanket is a soft toy. Mr. Blanket has never been washed. Mr. Blanket has a smell your toddler describes as "home."

outcomes.text: Four loads. Your toddler watches Mr. Blanket tumble in the dryer window like a hostage video. He comes out warm, clean and, according to your toddler, "wrong."

choices.label: Text your partner: laundry tonight is theirs

outcomes.text: "On it." Four loads after bedtime, folded, Mr. Blanket included. You find him on your pillow at 10 PM, still warm. You are not crying. It's the steam.
"I did laundry Sunday." It was one load, of their gym clothes. You don't say that. You think it, at a volume they can probably hear.

choices.label: Just the sheets. Mr. Blanket stays feral.

outcomes.text: Sheets on hot. Mr. Blanket stays fragrant and untouched. If daycare ever asks, he was washed, and you will lie to a teacher's face.

events.title: Is That Eye Pink?
events.text: Your toddler rubs one eye. You freeze. You hold their face under the kitchen light like a jeweler with a stolen diamond. It looks eye-colored? Probably? You've stared so long you've forgotten what eyes look like.

choices.label: Call the nurse line, just to be sure

outcomes.text: The nurse asks four calm questions. No redness, no goop, no fever. "Sounds like a tired eye." Your toddler says "hi" to the nurse eleven times. You thank them like someone pulled from the sea.
"Looks like an eye. A very cute eye." Ten minutes later: "Called the nurse line from the stairwell. Tired eye. We're fine." You read "we're" four times.
"?" Then "looks fine??" Then "in a meeting." Three texts, two question marks, no help. You call the nurse line yourself, slightly louder than you need to.

choices.label: Post it to the group chat for a vote

outcomes.text: Eleven parents vote. Six say pink, four say fine, one sends a link to an eye oil. The daycare director has seen it now. The director has questions about tomorrow.

events.title: The Bite
events.text: Mid-cuddle, your toddler bites your shoulder. Not a nibble. A full, molar-assisted chomp, with eye contact. Then a giggle, because your face just did something it has never done before.

choices.label: Calmly: "Ouch. Teeth are for the teether."

outcomes.text: You swap your shoulder for a cold teether and say it like a nature documentary. They chomp the teether instead. Lesson received, for the next ten minutes.
They bite the teether, then you, then the teether, as if comparing. You come in second. It stings in a whole new way.
It is the funniest thing that has ever happened. They bite again for an encore. The encore is mostly [BLEEP]. You are now a squeaky toy with a mortgage.

choices.label: Frozen teether and a pouch. Buy some peace.

outcomes.text: One cold ring, one $2.99 pouch. Silence, chewing, a small sigh from you both. Then the pouch gets squeezed into the couch. Your shoulder has a perfect dental record on it.

events.title: Bib Number Seven
events.text: Bib number seven. The drool is industrial. Your toddler's chin is red and chapped, your shoulder is damp, and the couch has a wet patch the shape of a small country.

outcomes.text: You apply balm 11 times. By the eleventh, they lift their chin for it, like a tiny boxer between rounds. The red fades. Your respect for boxing trainers grows.

choices.label: Text your partner: more bibs, the good balm

outcomes.text: They get home with bibs, balm and a frozen teething ring they bought without being asked. You consider proposing again.
"What kind of bibs?" "The bib kind." They get home with one bib. It has a lobster on it. It says "Shell Yeah." Technically, a bib.

choices.label: Let it drip. You live in a swamp now.

outcomes.text: You stop fighting it. Everything you own is slightly damp. The couch patch is now a large country, with a coastline.

events.title: Grandma Has Posted
events.text: Grandma has posted 41 photos of today. Number 23 is the toddler eating spaghetti with both fists, captioned "Somebody's parents let them eat like THIS 😂." It has 88 likes. Three are from the group chat.

choices.label: Call her. Ask her to take that one down.

outcomes.text: She takes it down. She posts a new one: "Not allowed to share the spaghetti one 🙄." It has more likes than the spaghetti did.
"Of course, sweetheart," she says, and takes it down, in a voice so sincere you check it for traps. There are no traps. You're too tired to trust that.
Spin control. Two parents like your comment. One replies "lol the spaghetti 😂." You have made it a thread. Threads are forever.
"LOL. Honestly, the spaghetti looks great." A small, private laugh between the two people who actually run this place.
"Well, did you let them eat like that?" You did. They know you did. You put the phone face-down, very gently, like it might go off.

events.title: "Oh, You Cut Them THAT Way"
events.text: At dinner, Grandma watches your partner cut the toddler's noodles into small, sensible pieces. "Oh," she says, to no one, to everyone. "You cut them THAT way." The knife stops.

outcomes.text: Grandma raises both hands, the picture of innocence. The knife resumes. Later, Grandma tells the family group chat you've been "very sensitive lately."

choices.label: Laugh along. They do cut them a bit small.

outcomes.text: Grandma beams. Your partner's knife stays very still. You will hear about this at 10:40 PM, in a whisper, in the dark.

choices.label: Ask Grandma about her knee. All of it.

outcomes.text: Thirty minutes on the knee: the surgeon, the parking, the physical therapist who "isn't a real doctor." Your partner finishes dinner in peace and squeezes your hand under the table.

events.title: Sticker Inflation
events.text: The deal was one sticker per potty. Your toddler has renegotiated: two stickers, a cracker and "the big song." The chart on the fridge now looks like a bank in a history documentary.

choices.label: Hold the line: one sticker, no song

outcomes.text: They accept the terms, sulk, and go anyway. One sticker. You feel like a central banker who did the hard thing.
They go on strike. The strike takes place on the kitchen floor, with eye contact.

choices.label: Two stickers and a cracker. Inflation is real.

outcomes.text: It works too well. They now go in tiny installments, for maximum stickers. Nine before lunch. You're out of dinosaurs and down to the dentist's smiley faces.

choices.label: Full potty parade for every success

outcomes.text: You march. You sing. You play a kazoo you didn't know you owned. They're so into it they go twice. You're so into it you pull something in your hip.

events.title: Bare-Bottom Afternoon
events.text: The method says: no pants, lots of water, watch for "the signs." Your toddler is pantsless, hydrated and showing the signs either constantly or never. You've watched a small bottom for 40 minutes like a lighthouse keeper.

outcomes.text: Ding. Sprint. Success! You cheer so loudly a dog two houses down joins in. Your toddler takes a bow, which, given the outfit, is a lot.
Between dings: the couch. The good couch. Twelve seconds after the last trip, with total confidence.
The man in corduroy sings about rain. Your toddler sits perfectly still on the couch. Stillness, it turns out, is exactly when it happens. The cushion cover goes in the wash.

choices.label: Towels on every surface. Every one.

outcomes.text: Fourteen towels. The living room looks like a spa run by raccoons. It works: everything lands on terry cloth. You now have fourteen towels to wash.

events.title: The Sitter Has a Few Questions
events.text: The sitter texts: "Hi!! Few q's for tonight 😊" Then eleven questions, numbered. Number 7 is "do u have snacks for me." Number 11 is "Anything else I should know?" There is so much else.

choices.label: Write the full guide. Two pages. Bullet points.

outcomes.text: Routine, snacks, the Song (lyrics attached), where the backup lovey hides, what "the blue thing" means. The sitter replies "omg ur so organized." You're not. You're terrified.

choices.label: Answer number 7. The rest is vibes.

outcomes.text: "Snacks in the pantry. They'll be asleep. They may tell you about a bird." The sitter replies "ok!" with an energy you'll think about during dessert.

choices.label: Ask your partner to call the sitter

outcomes.text: They call. They go through all eleven and add a twelfth about the nightlight. You hear them say "we" a lot. You like hearing them say it.
"Can you? You know the routine." They're not wrong. That's the trap with the routine: you're the one who knows it. You answer all eleven, plus a twelfth nobody asked.

events.title: The Going-Out Shirt
events.text: Your going-out shirt has been in a drawer since spring. It has a crease like a folded map, a stain like a smaller map and, as of four minutes ago, a toddler wearing it as a cape.

choices.label: Iron it properly. Treat the stain. Be a person.

outcomes.text: Stain stick, steam, a second pass. It looks almost new, in low light, which the restaurant will provide. You hold it up like a trophy you ironed yourself.

choices.label: Dryer, damp towel, ten minutes. Pray.

outcomes.text: The crease is 60% gone. The stain is now baked in, a permanent feature. You'll keep an arm over it all night like a nervous senator.

choices.label: Wear the sweater. The sweater is always fine.

outcomes.text: The sweater has seen four Fridays like this one. Your partner will say "The sweater, huh?" in a voice that's either fond or not. You won't ask which.

events.title: Reservation Confirmed
events.text: Your partner texts: "Confirmed for 7:30!! 🎉" Then: "I could leave work at 3:30 so you can rest? I'd have to log back on later, but." The "but" just sits there. It's a real offer. It's also a real but.

outcomes.text: They're home by 4. You lie in a dark room for 40 minutes like a phone on a charger. When you get up, the toddler has "helped" fold laundry, which means unfolded it.
They're home at 4:40 and back on the laptop by 4:45. "I'm here, though!" they say, from behind a screen. Technically, they are.
You've got it. You absolutely have it. At 4:30 you're on the floor looking for a shoe, and you have it, and your partner sends a heart, and that has to count for something.

events.title: The Chair Is Moving
events.text: From the kitchen comes the scrape of a chair being dragged, slowly and with purpose, toward the counter. Like a very small mover with a plan.

outcomes.text: You arrive as a small hand reaches the flour. You lift them down mid-reach. They look at you like you've cancelled their show.

choices.label: Five more minutes on the couch

outcomes.text: The scraping stops. Peace. Wonderful, suspicious peace.

events.title: It's Snowing in the Kitchen
events.text: The flour canister is open. Your toddler stands in a small, private blizzard, delighted, making snow angels on the tile.

outcomes.text: You sweep, then wipe, then sweep the wipe. Flour is in places flour has never been. You'll find it in your ear on Thursday.

choices.label: Call it a sensory bin, officially

outcomes.text: You add measuring cups and lean in. A craft board would call this "open-ended play." It is mostly open-ended flour.

choices.label: Close the kitchen door. Future you's problem.

outcomes.text: Future you is going to be so annoyed. Future you should have thought of that.

events.title: The Bathroom Door Is Closed
events.text: The bathroom door, which you left open, is now closed. From the inside. Someone in there is humming.

outcomes.text: Inside: a toddler holding the toothpaste like a microphone, cap already off. You take it. They give a small, professional bow.
Everyone deserves a little alone time. You get some too. It lasts four minutes.

events.title: Minty Fresh
events.text: The mirror, the sink, the bath mat and the toddler are now toothpaste. The bathroom smells like a dentist's dream. There is some on the ceiling. How.

outcomes.text: Twenty minutes with a sponge. The bathroom has never been cleaner, or mintier. The ceiling remains a mystery.
It is not basically soap. It dries into a crust that will outlive you both.

events.title: The Safety Scissors Are Missing
events.text: The craft drawer is open. The round-tipped safety scissors are gone. So is your toddler, from this room.

outcomes.text: Under the dining table: scissors open, a fistful of their own bangs, not yet cut. You trade the scissors for a crayon. Close one.

choices.label: They're safety scissors. How bad can it be?

outcomes.text: You finish your email. From under the dining table: one distant, satisfied snip.

events.title: The Haircut
events.text: Your toddler has given themselves bangs. One side only. Very short. They are thrilled. You look at the picture-day flyer on the fridge.

choices.label: Take them to a kids' salon to even it out

outcomes.text: The stylist sighs, "Happens every week," and evens it out. It's even now. Even shorter. $28 and a lollipop.

choices.label: Post it before anyone else can

outcomes.text: "Our little stylist ✂️" Thirty-one laughing faces. One parent asks, sincerely, who you went to.

events.title: The Shark and the Laptop
events.text: Your laptop is open on the coffee table with the report on screen. Your toddler is circling it slowly, like a shark that has read about laptops.

outcomes.text: Click. The shark looks at you, then at the closed laptop, then swims off in search of a softer target.

choices.label: They can't reach the keyboard. Probably.

outcomes.text: You use the time to stare into the open fridge. It's lovely in there. Cold and quiet.

events.title: Report Submitted
events.text: Your toddler has added nine pages of the letter J and a winky face to the report, then pressed every key, including the one that sends it to your whole team.

choices.label: Redo the edits. Send a sheepish v2.

outcomes.text: "Please disregard the previous version." You delete 4,000 Js one by one, like a monk with a grudge.
Two coworkers laugh. Two coworkers also have kids at your daycare. It's in the group chat by lunch.

events.title: "I Don't Need to Go."
events.text: "I don't need to go," your toddler says, doing a small, urgent dance. "I don't need to go," they repeat, crossing their legs.

outcomes.text: You make it with two seconds to spare. A success! You both cheer. You cheer harder.
They're a person. They know their own body. You respect that, and sit down for the first time since 6.

events.title: The Good Rug
events.text: The good rug. The rug from before you had a toddler, back when you had opinions about rugs. The rug has been christened.

outcomes.text: Enzyme spray, a towel, your whole body weight. It's mostly out. The rug will never be the good rug again, but it'll be a rug.
The living room is a bare, echoing floor now. It looks like a dance studio. Your toddler takes this as a challenge.

events.title: A Soft, Papery Crunch
events.text: Your toddler has gone quiet in the corner and is chewing something with real dedication. You hear a soft, papery crunch.

outcomes.text: It's the library book. You swap it for a frozen teether. They accept the trade like a fair businessperson.
The whimpering stops. Something is working. You decide not to know what.

events.title: Library Property
events.text: The library book about a tired bear now has a bite-shaped bay where the bear used to be. The sticker on the back says "Damaged items will be billed."

outcomes.text: The librarian has seen worse. The librarian has a form for this. You fill out the form while your toddler chews the pen.
Tape, hope and a strategic bookmark. They will find out. Libraries always find out.

events.title: The Chirp
events.text: Somewhere in the house, a smoke detector is chirping for a new battery, once every forty seconds. You can't tell which one. Your toddler starts chirping back.

outcomes.text: You find it on the fourth ladder climb and change the battery, because that part matters. Your toddler keeps chirping for two days.

events.title: Pajama Day Was Today
events.text: The group chat posts 31 photos of tiny pajamas. Today was pajama day at daycare. Your toddler was the only one in jeans and a very serious sweater.

outcomes.text: Someone replies, "Aw, they looked so professional!" with no emoji. You will think about it in the shower for a week.

events.title: Since Breakfast
events.text: You catch your reflection in a shop window. There's yogurt in your hair. Judging by the crust, it's been there since breakfast. You've talked to six people today.

outcomes.text: Six people. Nobody said anything. That's either kindness or a group decision.

events.title: The Kitchen Has Been Improved
events.text: Grandma has reorganized your kitchen. It's efficient. It's logical. It has labels. You will never find the colander again.

outcomes.text: She glows. You look for a spoon nine times today. The spoons are in a drawer labeled "SPOONS." You never once think to look there.
She shows you. Then she tells the family group chat you were "a little short" with her. Your cousin reacts with a 😬.

events.title: Your Eye Itches
events.text: Your toddler is fine. Your eye, however, has itched for an hour and is now the color of a stop sign. Daycare's pink eye has found a new host: you.

outcomes.text: A video visit, a prescription, a pharmacy run with a toddler. Drops twice a day. Wash your hands. Wash them again.

choices.label: Sunglasses, indoors, like a celebrity in hiding

outcomes.text: You wear sunglasses to the mailbox. A neighbor asks if you're okay, in a voice that has already decided.

events.title: Twelve Eggs, One Floor
events.text: You turned your back for the length of one sneeze. The fridge is open. The egg carton is open. The floor is a breakfast you didn't make.

outcomes.text: Raw egg does not wipe. Raw egg relocates. Fifteen minutes later the floor is clean and you are not.

choices.label: Let them "help" with the paper towels

outcomes.text: They help. They are so proud. The egg is now spread across a wider, more ambitious area.

choices.label: Towel over it. Deal with it after nap.

outcomes.text: The towel is a lid on a problem. By 3 PM the kitchen has a smell with a personality.

events.title: Rex Went Swimming
events.text: A flush. A gurgle. A small voice: "Rex went swimming." Rex is a plastic dinosaur. The toilet is now a tide pool, and the tide is coming in.

outcomes.text: The plumber fishes Rex out with a tool like a robot arm and charges $240. Rex is fine. The bathroom floor is not. Your wallet is in intensive care.

choices.label: Plunger, gloves and a video tutorial

outcomes.text: Forty minutes, one snake from the hardware store and a noise you'll never forget. Rex emerges. Your toddler greets Rex like a returning astronaut.
The tutorial man made it look easy. The tutorial man had a different toilet. You call the plumber anyway, now with wet sleeves.

choices.label: Close the lid. Sign on the door. Later.

outcomes.text: "CLOSED FOR RENOVATIONS." You are a one-toilet household now, like pioneers. Rex is lost at sea, and your toddler is in mourning.

events.title: Daycare Is Calling
events.text: Daycare: "They're running a fever of 101. Can you come within the hour?" You are, at this exact moment, unmuting yourself to present the numbers.

outcomes.text: You leave mid-slide. Your toddler is flushed, floppy and very glad to see you. Fluids, rest, the dose on the fridge. The numbers will have to wait.

choices.label: Ask your partner to get them

outcomes.text: "Leaving now." Your partner gets there in twenty minutes. You present to a room of nodding faces while texting "thank you" under the table.
"I'm in a thing too." Of course they are. You both leave your things. You both resent it. You both drive.
Nine minutes of slides, then a dash. You make it in fifty-eight minutes. The director's face says "fifty-eight" back to you.

events.title: A Note From Daycare
events.text: "A case of head lice has been reported in the Caterpillar Room." You read it twice. Your scalp begins to itch immediately and will not stop until Sunday.

outcomes.text: The fine-tooth comb, every head, every pillowcase on hot. You find nothing. You keep looking. You will dream about combs.

choices.label: Split it with your partner tonight

outcomes.text: You comb, they wash. Two adults in headlamps at 8 PM, whispering "anything?" It's almost romantic. It isn't. But almost.
"Can't it wait till the weekend?" It cannot. You do it alone, loudly, so they can hear the combing.
A calm professional with a magnifying lamp combs your toddler while they watch cartoons. $180. Someone from daycare recognizes your car in the lot.

events.title: Locked Out
events.text: You step onto the porch for the package. Behind you: click. Through the glass, your toddler waves, safe inside and thrilled, one hand still on the lock.

choices.label: Yell for the neighbor with the spare key

outcomes.text: You stay at the window making faces while the neighbor jogs over in a bathrobe with the spare key. They will tell this at every block party, forever. Inside, the snack drawer has been emptied.
"Turn the little thing. The LITTLE thing." Ninth try: click. You cheer. They cheer. They lock it again, then unlock it, beaming.
They wave. They blow a kiss. They wander off to empty the snack drawer. Twenty minutes in, you yell for the neighbor anyway.

events.title: Grandpa Was Mid-Story
events.text: Your in-laws' weekly video call. Grandpa is describing his gutters when your toddler leans into frame and projectile-vomits directly onto the laptop.

outcomes.text: You hang up mid-gutter. Towels, bath, clean pajamas, a cool cloth. Your toddler perks up at once. The laptop does not.

choices.label: Point the camera at the ceiling: "Bad connection!"

outcomes.text: Grandpa finishes the gutter story to your ceiling fan while you clean one-handed. You hear him say "Hello?" eleven times.

choices.label: Pass the call to your partner

outcomes.text: Your partner takes the laptop and the parents; you take the toddler. A pit crew. A disgusting, efficient pit crew.
Your partner is in the shower and stays there. You do both, badly. Grandpa sees things.

events.title: The Car Won't Start
events.text: Toddler buckled. Bag packed. Snacks loaded. You turn the key. Click. Click. Nothing. In the back seat, a shoe comes off, then the other shoe, then a sock.

outcomes.text: You unbuckle them first, obviously, and wait inside. "About an hour" is two. You play I spy at the window until you've spied everything twice.

choices.label: Flag down a neighbor for a jump

outcomes.text: A neighbor with jumper cables and a lot of confidence. It works on the fourth try. They explain alternators to you for twenty minutes.

choices.label: Unbuckle. Walk wherever you were going.

outcomes.text: You walk. They ride on your shoulders, then walk, then insist on carrying the bag. You arrive late, sweaty and somehow closer.

events.title: A Small Hand
events.text: Halfway down the block, without being asked, your toddler reaches up and takes your hand. Not for the crossing. Not for anything. Just to hold it.

outcomes.text: You walk at their speed, which is the speed of noticing things. A leaf. A cat in a window. Their hand stays in yours the whole way.

choices.label: Tell your partner about it tonight

outcomes.text: That night you tell them. They go quiet, then say, "They did that to me last week." You both sit with it for a while.

events.title: The Song, Sung Back
events.text: From the next room you hear your toddler singing the bedtime song to their stuffed rabbit. Your song. They get most of the words right, and the tune exactly.

choices.label: Stand in the doorway and listen

outcomes.text: You don't go in. You stay just out of sight until the last line. The rabbit is tucked in under a dish towel. Somebody taught them that. You did.
Thirty-one seconds of shaky video. Your partner watches it four times on their lunch break and replies, "I'm not crying, you're crying."

events.title: Half a Cracker
events.text: You're sitting on the kitchen floor, out of steam. Your toddler studies your face, breaks their cracker in half, and gives you the bigger piece.

outcomes.text: You eat your half. They eat theirs. They pat your knee twice, like a doctor who has seen enough. You feel better. You really do.
"WHAT," your partner replies, then: "They've never shared with me." Then: "Proud of both of you."

events.title: "Thank You, Bus Driver"
events.text: As the bus doors open, your toddler turns to the driver and says, clearly and unprompted, "Thank you, bus driver." The driver puts a hand on their heart.

outcomes.text: "That was really kind." They nod, very serious, and say "kind" back to you, trying the word on. It fits.

choices.label: Save it for the dinner table

outcomes.text: At dinner you tell your partner, and the toddler says "thank you, bus driver" again, for an audience this time. You both clap.

events.title: Asleep on You
events.text: Mid-story on the couch, your toddler goes heavy and warm against your chest and falls asleep. Their breathing slows. Yours does too.

choices.label: Stay still. Stay awake. Just be here.

outcomes.text: Twenty minutes of the most important nothing. You count their eyelashes. You remember the hospital. You don't move until they do.

choices.label: Ease them into bed and send your partner a photo

outcomes.text: The transfer works. You send a photo of the small, sleeping face. "Coming home early," your partner writes. They mean it.

events.title: All the Voices
events.text: From the hallway you watch your partner read to the toddler. They're doing all the voices, badly and wholeheartedly. The toddler is gazing up at them like they invented books.

outcomes.text: You take the bear's lines. Your partner keeps the owl. The toddler laughs at the owl every single time. For ten minutes, the three of you are a whole show.

choices.label: Lean on the doorframe and watch

outcomes.text: You don't interrupt. You just watch the person you chose being good at this. Later you tell them so, and they look surprised, and pleased.

events.title: The Blue Cup
events.text: 1:58 AM. "Wa-wa." Not water in general. Water in the blue cup. The blue cup is in the dishwasher, which is running, which was your idea.

choices.label: Bring water in the green cup. Sell it.

outcomes.text: You hand over the green cup like it was always the plan. They sip, study it like a wine they didn't order, and accept. Confidence is most of parenting.
Your partner gets up, fishes the blue cup out of a running dishwasher by feel and rinses it in the dark. You hear all of it. A quiet hero. You'll say thank you at 7.
"You're closer," they mumble. You are not closer. You are both exactly the same distance from the door. You go anyway, because one of you has to.
"Wa-wa" four more times, each one quieter. Then a long sigh, like a landlord giving up. Silence. You won by doing nothing, which never happens.
"Wa-wa" becomes "WA-WA" becomes a song about wa-wa. You get up and stand at the sink at 2:09 AM, rinsing a cup out of a dishwasher mid-cycle.

events.title: Night Vision
events.text: 2:31 AM. On the monitor, in grainy green, your toddler is sitting bolt upright and staring directly into the camera. Not crying. Not moving. Waiting.

choices.label: Go in and see what they want

outcomes.text: They need to tell you, urgently, that they have a foot. You confirm the foot. They lie down, satisfied. You lie awake for an hour, less satisfied.
Your partner looks at the screen, says "Nope," and then goes anyway, because they can count. The ledger has spoken, and it speaks for you tonight.
Your partner opens one eye, runs the ledger in their head and closes the eye again. Fair. You go, muttering, which is also fair.
You flip it back over ten minutes later. They're asleep, sitting up, chin on chest, like a commuter. Good enough.
Face-down, it can still hear. "HELLO?" it says, in a very small voice. Then louder. You go in, and they wave like you're late for a meeting.

events.title: Rabbit Overboard
events.text: 3:20 AM. The stuffed rabbit has gone over the side of the crib. It is eight inches from their hand. It might as well be on the moon. The wailing is operatic.

choices.label: Return the rabbit. No eye contact.

outcomes.text: In and out in 40 seconds, like a pit crew. They grab the rabbit, sigh and are asleep before you reach the door. A personal best nobody saw.
Your partner goes. Through the wall: a creak, a whispered "here's Bun," a door. They're back and asleep in nine seconds. You'll find that annoying tomorrow.
"Rabbit," you whisper. "Rabbit," they whisper back, and don't move. A standoff. You lose the standoff. You always lose the standoff.
They don't find the rabbit. They find their own foot, decide it will do, and fall asleep holding it.
